Q: Extra Row with blank values created with MS Graph when inserting into Sharepoint List A:

From what you've shared, I don't see anything in the code that would cause PostAsync() to create two items. That call should only send a single POST request to Microsoft Graph.

Since you've already confirmed the method is only being hit once, I'd start looking outside the C# code. A few things worth checking:

  • Whether there's a Power Automate flow or SharePoint workflow that's triggered when an item is created.

  • Any event receivers, webhooks, or customizations on the site that might be creating another item.

  • Enable Graph SDK logging (or use a tool like Fiddler) to verify that only one HTTP POST is actually leaving your application.

If only one request is being sent but two items appear in the list, then the extra blank item is likely being created on the SharePoint side rather than by your code.

Nothing in the request body you've posted looks like it would explain the duplicate insert, especially if similar code works correctly with other lists.

just copy the shortcut, rename it to indicate x64 and then replace the target executable path to "%SystemRoot%\system32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" which will be your 64bit version on a 64bit Windows system.

Q: How to achieve a blur effect in PHP? A:

I've tried many answers, but I've obtained best results and best scalability with the Imagick PHP extension. Example PHP code:

$imagick = new Imagick('a.jpeg');
$imagick->blurImage(0, 6.0); // Radius, sigma
$imagick->writeImage('a.jpeg');
$imagick->clear();

Original image:

To:

To have more blur, just increase the 6.0 sigma parameter.

Disadvantages:

  • you need to install the Imagick extension (sudo apt install php-imagick or similar)

Advantages:

  • more efficient than exec() and convert etc. - as it's native PHP, not a shell command
  • much more efficient than calling many times the imagefilter($image, IMG_FILTER_GAUSSIAN_BLUR); - for example I migrated away from a code which was calling this method 40 times to achieve similar results, but with much slower

Credits: https://stackoverflow.com/a/14428602/3451846 https://www.php.net/manual/en/imagick.blurimage.php
